title: An Emu in the Sky over Paranal
caption: The Coalsack Nebula and the Magellanic Clouds over the Very Large Telescope, Paranal Observatory, Chile
celestial: Photograph taken at Paranal Observatory, Chile

recognition.text: ESO Picture of the Week (an editorial selection, not an audience score).

story: Two of the Very Large Telescope's Unit Telescopes sit quietly on Cerro Paranal, bathed in starlight, as the Milky Way arches over ESO's Paranal Observatory. Between the two telescopes shine the Small and Large Magellanic Clouds. Above the telescope on the left, the Coalsack Nebula lies across the Milky Way as a dark smudge, like a giant thumbprint.

The Magellanic Clouds belong to the Local Group, the family of galaxies that includes our own. The Large Cloud lies 163 000 light-years from the Milky Way and the Small Cloud 200 000 light-years. The Coalsack is practically next door by comparison, roughly 600 light-years from the Solar System, and no other dark nebula is as easy to see in our skies.

Many ancient cultures recorded it. To several indigenous Australian groups it forms the head of the Emu in the Sky. Aboriginal Australians are probably the oldest astronomers in the world, and they define constellations using dark nebulae rather than stars, unlike the Western tradition.
scale: The Coalsack Nebula lies roughly 600 light-years from the Solar System, according to ESO.

understand.summary: This is a ground-based landscape photograph by Yuri Beletsky. The source does not publish camera, exposure or color-processing details.
understand.eye: The Coalsack is dark to eye and camera alike, but a camera gathering light over time may show the surrounding Milky Way and the Magellanic Clouds more brightly than an observer would see them.

explore: Such dark clouds stand out more in the southern sky than in the north, and other cultures drew dark constellations too. For Inca astronomers, an especially important one was Urcuchillay, the Llama, reflecting how much the animals mattered as a source of food, wool and transport. ESO photo ambassador Yuri Beletsky took the picture.
alt: The Milky Way arching over two large telescope enclosures, with two fuzzy patches between them and a dark smudge across the Milky Way above the left telescope.
